s010.line: You snap at Jay, your best friend.

s027.line: Her number does not move. Still three.
The number does not listen to words.

s052.line: The ones with her name on them.

s057.line: She stops asking you for things.

s059.line: You watch her number like a clock.

s061.line: I can see your patience running out?

s063.line: Science says a new habit takes sixty-six days.
Sixty-six days to build one good habit.

s064.line: One bad moment takes one second.
That is the math. One second to break it.

s067.line: Day two: you walk your sister home.

s071.line: Your mom smiles when you come home.

s073.line: He does not reply. But he reads it.

s077.line: The one he told you in confidence.
The one about his dad leaving.

s078.line: You say it like a joke.

s079.line: He is standing right behind you.

s082.line: The pill does not turn red.
It does not flash. It just disappears.

s083.line: He does not hit you. He just walks away.

s084.line: He does not answer your texts.
At school, he looks through you.

s087.line: Done is quiet. Done does not slam doors.

s092.line: The old man does not shout.
He just sits down. He looks out the window.

s093.line: He is used to it. That is the worst part.
He is used to being done with.

s095.line: But you are the reason someone else looks like that now.

s097.line: On your street, a couple argues on a porch.

s099.line: He stands there, hands in his pockets.
Nobody leaves. But something left anyway.

s100.line: You keep walking. Every street has a number falling somewhere.

s101.line: You count them as you pass.

s104.line: Four chances left with the people who matter.

s105.line: You did not lose Jay's number.
You lost a piece of your own.

s106.line: Your mom asks about your day.

s107.line: You are tired. You are scared.

s108.line: She goes quiet. Her number was three.

s109.line: You watch it drop and you cannot stop it.
The number does not move. It never moves up.

s111.line: You have spent your whole life thinking people would always be there.

s117.line: You keep going. You bring his homework.
You leave it at the door.

s119.line: Day eight: his little brother opens the door.

s120.line: Day nine: you leave a note.
I was wrong. Forgive me later.

s121.line: Day ten: you fix his bike chain.

s124.line: Showing up is not a trick.
It is not a key. It is just showing up.

s124b.line: You do not ask for a chance.
You do not say sorry. You just show up.

s126.line: She looks at you for a long time.
Then she says: he is in the backyard.

s129.line: He sees you. He does not smile.
He does not walk away either.

s130.line: He bounces the ball to you.

s131.line: No number above his head. No pill.
Just a ball. Rolling to your feet.

s132.line: And you understand. Zero was not the end.
Zero was the end of counting.

s133.line: What comes after zero is not a number.
It is a choice. His choice. Not yours.

s136.line: No one says sorry. No one has to.

s137.line: That night you call your mom.

s140.line: Your number never goes back up.
It stays four. It will always stay four.

s142.line: The point is: you cannot earn a chance back.
You can only earn the next one.

s143.line: So spend every chance like it is your last.
